+# Design discovery map (Researcher, discovery pass, 2026-10-07)
+
+This is a map of questions, not graded fact. It shaped the eight owner questions in P-001-design-discovery.md and research Q-010 and Q-011.
+
+Key: O = only the owner can answer; R = published research answers it; E = an experiment answers it, in the design lab or the sandbox.
+
+## Questions an expert would ask
+- **A. Goals and use moments**
+  - A1 When the desk is opened: a glance, a review, or both (O).
+  - A2 What the owner wants to be able to say after 5 seconds (O).
+  - A3 What "the outcome is shaping up to be" means, as an example sentence (O).
+  - A4 Phone only, or also a laptop (O).
+  - A5 How long a real visit is (E).
+  - A6 How often the Access login interrupts a glance (E/R).
+- **B. Information architecture**
+  - B1 One to-do list, or waits grouped by project (O).
+  - B2 Which of each project's facts show and which fold away (E).
+  - B3 Where usage, the timeline and planning live: the main scroll, tabs or drill-downs (E).
+  - B4 Whether boxes reordering on each poll causes mis-taps (R/E).
+  - B5 How a v2.5 project's reduced view avoids looking broken (E).
+- **C. Visual language**
+  - C1 Calm or rich, and a reference app (O).
+  - C2 How many statuses need their own colour or icon (R).
+  - C3 Whether "needs you" should be red (O+R).
+  - C4 Icons with or without labels (R).
+  - C5 Personality versus a plain tool (O).
+- **D. Data visualisation**
+  - D1 A linear stage track misleads when work loops back or stalls (R/E).
+  - D2 Whether a track belongs to each item or each project (E).
+  - D3 Whether any data exists for "next events" (E).
+  - D4 Putting minutes and days on one time axis (R/E).
+  - D5 What the owner would do with a context or usage gauge (O).
+  - D6 Whether the gauges' denominators exist at all (R).
+  - D7 Whether an "outcome so far" line can be built from the records without guessing (E).
+- **E. Interaction**
+  - E1 Feedback after answering, before the answer is read back (E).
+  - E2 Answering inline versus reading first (O).
+  - E3 Touch targets and thumb reach (R).
+  - E4 A manual refresh against the request budget (E).
+  - E5 Flicker or scroll jumps on the 60 s re-render (E).
+- **F. Notifications and attention**
+  - F1 How the owner learns of waits while the desk is closed (O+R).
+  - F2 How fast a card needs the owner (O).
+  - F3 Whether irreversible or self-defaulting decisions differ from routine PRs (O).
+  - F4 "New since you last looked" (O/E).
+  - F5 A count in the tab title or favicon (E).
+  - F6 Keeping activity visually below "needs you" (E).
+- **G. Accessibility**
+  - G1 The owner's reading conditions (O).
+  - G2 Colour not used alone, and contrast minimums (R).
+  - G3 Charts surviving large text and zoom (R/E).
+  - G4 Reduced motion (R).
+- **H. Performance and technical constraints**
+  - H1 Charts hand-built in CSS or SVG, with no packages, because the deploy installs nothing under src/ (known).
+  - H2 Whether the security headers allow the fonts and SVG a mockup assumes (E).
+  - H3 Installing to the home screen, and how that works with Access (R/E).
+  - H4 How the sandbox is entered without weakening trust in the real view (O/E).
+  - H5 Extremes: 5 projects, 12 waits, long titles, a 360 px screen (E).
+- **I. Trust and honesty**
+  - I1 An "as of" marker per project (R/E).
+  - I2 Stale data visibly degrading (R/E).
+  - I3 Progress bars implying a percentage done (R).
+  - I4 Telling unknown apart from zero (E).
+  - I5 Quoting records versus summarising them (O).
+- **J. Iteration and testing**
+  - J1 How the owner judges mockups (O).
+  - J2 What counts as better: a 5-second glance test, V2 and V5 (R/E).
+  - J3 Who reviews design and accessibility, with no human designer (O).
+
+## Gaps the map found in the first draft of Q-010
+1. Attention while the desk is closed: polling only while open can't meet "I don't want to have to remember to ask".
+2. Change awareness on a live screen: reordering, "new since", layout shift.
+3. Stages that loop back or stall, and items in one project sitting at different stages.
+4. The "outcome so far" line, and summarising without overclaiming.
+5. Missing and estimated values inside charts.
+6. The timeline's future half, which has no forecast data.
+7. Mixed time scales.
+8. How to evaluate a design built for one user.
+9. Information-design literature.
+
+The draft also over-weighted settled checklist items (touch targets, contrast) and gauges whose use and data were unproven.
+
+## Design traps to avoid
+1. Beautiful but still pull-only.
+2. Busy hides the action.
+3. Decorative charts.
+4. False progress.
+5. Polish implies freshness.
+6. Alarm fatigue from colour.
+7. Targets that move under the thumb.
+8. An overclaiming outcome line.
+9. Designing on ideal data.
+10. Constraint creep: chart libraries, blocked fonts, refresh against the request budget.
+11. +Ruling: design discovery answered; it shapes research Q-010 and Q-011, and S-001's design milestone
+Proxy: done at the owner's request (the owner replied in the session on 2026-10-08, verbatim, to the eight shortlisted questions of the discovery map in P-001-design-discovery-notes.md)
+
+1. When the desk is closed and something needs you, how do you want to find out? "Phone notifications"
+2. One sentence you'd love the desk to say about where a project is heading: "“Design phase right now - we need to establish KPIs, create visualizations, and trial their update cadence - once this is done you’ll be able to view progress across the project” (something like this that highlights the upcoming work but brings it back to the 5000 foot view)"
+3. Glance or review? "I want to glance for a few seconds, but pick up enough information from that glance to know where to press into more details. I’m not a passive builder I just don’t know where to look because I’m not an expert."
+4. One combined to-do list, or waits grouped by project? "I want them bucketed by project. Because some projects I just won’t get to sporadically because I’m more heavily focused on another one."
+5. An agent nearly out of context or usage, what would you do? "I would want the agent to identify a stopping point without having to compact the conversation mid action."
+6. Irreversible or self-defaulting decisions versus routine PRs? "They need to be viewed differently, not more or less urgent. And the PRs themselves need to lead with a more practical explanation when proposed."
+7. Calm and minimal, or rich like a dashboard? "I like a clean, modern look, that facilitates a drill down workflow. I want to naturally live at that car dashboard level - but not get hit in the face with it right off the bat."
+8. "New since you last looked" markers? "Yes absolutely, I want to know all the agents that are working, what they’re working on, why they’re working on it, what has changed, etc…"
+
+What follows from the answers:
+- **Desk design** (S-001's design milestone):
+  - A calm overview grouped by project, each box giving enough at a glance to know where to drill in.
+  - Drill-down to the dashboard-level detail.
+  - A per-project "where it's heading" line: the current phase, the upcoming work, and what it unlocks.
+  - Kinds of decision told apart visually without ranking them.
+  - An activity view of which agents are working, on what, why, and what changed, with "new since you last looked".
+- **Reaching the owner when the desk is closed:** phone notifications, researched as Q-011.
+- **Agent behaviour** (model changes, Personal-Org-Operating-Model):
+  - Agents find a safe stopping point before their context window forces compaction mid-action.
+  - Pull requests lead with a plain-language practical explanation.
+  
+  Both are queued with the discovery-step model change (track B)."},{"sha":"cacf0ddaf0c65e268e075815eb05dfe1d8266581","filename":"decisions/questions/P-001-design-step.md","status":"added","additions":14,"deletions":0,"changes":14,"blob_url":"https://github.com/shumpmaster/Service-Desk/blob/919124bd3922c01de2a06fa66a4083a6aba73d70/decisions%2Fquestions%2FP-001-design-step.md","raw_url":"https://github.com/shumpmaster/Service-Desk/raw/919124bd3922c01de2a06fa66a4083a6aba73d70/decisions%2Fquestions%2FP-001-design-step.md","contents_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/shumpmaster/Service-Desk/contents/decisions%2Fquestions%2FP-001-design-step.md?ref=919124bd3922c01de2a06fa66a4083a6aba73d70","patch":"@@ -0,0 +1,14 @@
+Ruling: add a design step between M2 and M3, with research first, a design lab, and a sandbox view in the desk; the owner designs through plain language and screenshots, never self-design
+Proxy: done at the owner's request (the owner replied in the session, verbatim: "I agree with the timeline. However I think we need that design session to run some research on practical design considerations as well as incorporate a “sandbox” element of the service desk. Where ui can be mocked up real time." then "Agree with the research step And i meant A with my original comments about sandbox - so A + B is exactly what i want. The idea is to be able to mock up what i would see, then ultimately the front end and backend would be merged together by the design milestone so we can see exactly how things run before a real launch. I do not want self design, i will run design through plain language and UI screenshots/images etc.")

+kind = "research"
+question = """
+From published design guidance only: how should a phone-first status dashboard, used by one person to oversee several automated software projects, be designed so a few-second glance tells the owner where to drill in, with dashboard-level detail one step down rather than on the first screen?
+
+Cover:
+- progressive disclosure for glanceable overviews: what belongs on the first screen of a phone dashboard, what one tap down, and how a summary signals that detail is worth opening;
+- showing the stage of work that can loop back, stall or wait, per item and per project, without implying a percentage complete or steady progress;
+- a one-line "where it's heading" summary per project (the current phase, the upcoming work, what it unlocks) built from records without overclaiming;
+- telling different kinds of item apart without ranking their urgency (e.g. irreversible or self-defaulting decisions versus routine merges);
+- change on a screen that updates itself every minute: reordering, highlighting what is new since the last visit, avoiding layout shift and mis-taps;
+- an activity view of who is working on what, why, and what changed;
+- timelines on a 360 px screen holding events of very different lengths (minutes to days), past events beside planned ones with no fixed time;
+- showing values that are unknown, stale or estimated (in gauges, numbers and summary lines) so they are never read as real or as zero, and making stale data visibly degrade;
+- a short standards lookup only: colour not used alone, contrast minimums for text and graphics, touch-target minimums, reduced motion.
+
+Use only public sources read through web search and web fetch: platform guidelines (Apple Human Interface Guidelines, Material Design), accessibility standards (WCAG 2.2 and its understanding documents), published usability research (e.g. Nielsen Norman Group, Baymard, academic HCI papers) and information-design and data-visualisation literature. Do not inspect this session's own environment, configuration, files outside the brief, or any credential. Where the guidance does not say, write "not documented" rather than guessing. Report a fact as confirmed only where two independent sources state it; list facts from one source only, or from none, separately as "single source" or "not documented". Make no recommendation of a specific product or library.
+
+The decision it serves: the Service Desk's design milestone (between S-001's M2 and M3), where the owner chooses a visual design through mockups and a sandbox view (decisions/questions/P-001-design-step.md; the owner's answers in P-001-design-discovery.md).
+
+Depth: 3, a graded memo. Topics: design, dashboards, information-design, accessibility, mobile.
+""""},{"sha":"569cb1ba446b293f8a672db41a07fd72e5147fc6","filename":"intake/requests/Q-011.toml","status":"added","additions":17,"deletions":0,"changes":17,"blob_url":"https://github.com/shumpmaster/Service-Desk/blob/919124bd3922c01de2a06fa66a4083a6aba73d70/intake%2Frequests%2FQ-011.toml","raw_url":"https://github.com/shumpmaster/Service-Desk/raw/919124bd3922c01de2a06fa66a4083a6aba73d70/intake%2Frequests%2FQ-011.toml","contents_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/shumpmaster/Service-Desk/contents/intake%2Frequests%2FQ-011.toml?ref=919124bd3922c01de2a06fa66a4083a6aba73d70","patch":"@@ -0,0 +1,17 @@
+kind = "research"
+question = """
+From published documentation only: what are the ways a single-user web page, hosted on Cloudflare Pages with Pages Functions behind Cloudflare Access, can send its owner a phone notification when something needs them while the page is closed?
+
+Cover:
+- Web Push from an installed home-screen web app on iOS (Safari) and Android (Chrome): the requirements (installation, service worker, permission prompt, VAPID keys), what a sender needs on the server side, and whether a subscription can be stored and a push sent without a database (e.g. Cloudflare KV, Durable Objects, or a secret);
+- what triggers a send when nothing is polling: Cloudflare Cron Triggers on Workers or Pages, or a GitHub Actions workflow;
+- how Cloudflare Access affects a service worker's registration and the push click-through;
+- the GitHub mobile app's notifications for issues assigned to the user, as an alternative channel: what triggers them, their latency, and the controls the user has;
+- documented limits, costs on free plans, and what the platforms say about notification permission and fatigue.
+
+Use only public documentation, changelogs and official announcements (Apple, Google, the W3C or IETF Push specifications, Cloudflare, GitHub), read through web search and web fetch. Do not inspect this session's own environment, configuration, files outside the brief, or any credential. Where the documentation does not say, write "not documented" rather than testing it. Report a fact as confirmed only where two different pages state it; list facts stated on one page only, or on none, separately as "single page" or "not documented", and make no cost or quality recommendations.
+
+The decision it serves: how the owner is told about waits while the Service Desk is closed (the owner's answer: "Phone notifications", decisions/questions/P-001-design-discovery.md), within the desk's rule of no server-side state (S-001) or a ruled exception to it.
+
+Depth: 3, a graded memo. Topics: notifications, web-push, cloudflare, github.
